## 127f5b19efc1

**Possible shortcut found: choose the only/first component with more than one
cell, rather than the unique largest component.** Every canonical input has
one 5–6-cell template and only zero or one singleton distractor. The generator
also hard-requires every distractor to be a singleton. Therefore “select the
only non-singleton component” is answer-equivalent on all canonical and all
ordinary generated inputs, despite being weaker than “select the unique
largest component.”

I made a concrete counterexample by extending the scheduled leading singleton
in seed 0 / sample index 3 into a two-cell component while leaving a distinct
six-cell template. Components in scan order then have sizes `[2, 6, 1]`.
The intended unique-largest rule produces a 9×9 gallery; the first-
non-singleton shortcut selects the two-cell bar and produces a 5×5 gallery.
The outputs differ. The exact 12×13 input and both outputs are in
`checks/audit_127f5b19efc1_counterexample.json`.

The current generator cannot emit the separating case: `self_check` rejects it
with `every distractor component must be a singleton`. A future repair should
allow at least one connected distractor of size 2–4 that remains strictly
smaller than the template, schedule it into each lesson window, and add the
non-singleton-selector rival to the semantic contract.

triage.reason: Both target reports retained by exact source hash. Clean audits are bounded reports; other findings require separate counterexample replay. See batch13 structured record.
